title: Intermittent "did not become stable" at init: `AppDriver$new()` navigates before the app's port is bound
description:
## Summary

An intermittent `AppDriver$new()` failure on a loaded CI runner — `Shiny app did not become stable in <load_timeout>ms` — traces back to how initialization decides the app is reachable. Initialization waits for the `Listening on http://…` line in the app's stderr ([`app_start_shiny()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3844574d93acfa6e3ae6fe25a41f5db5733ade2c/R/app-driver-start.R#L243-L245)) and then navigates the browser to the parsed URL. Per rstudio/shiny#4400, shiny prints that line one statement before it binds the socket, so on a slow or loaded host the navigation can reach a port that is not accepting yet: the browser lands on its network-error page, and when the app then binds, the error-page recovery navigation races the readiness/idle checks into the opaque "did not become stable" abort.

The abort is not a timeout — it fires within ~0.1s of a JavaScript exception, not at `load_timeout`. A deterministic reproducer, captured CI evidence, and the mechanism follow.

## Environment

- Packages: shinytest2 0.5.1, chromote 0.5.1, shiny 1.13.0; headless Chrome/Chromium.
- Seen on GitHub Actions (Linux, R-devel) under a loaded `R CMD check`; intermittent in the wild, reliably reproducible with the script below.

## Reproducer

This drives the normal entry point on a normal app; the only synthetic element is making shiny's announce→bind window deterministic (the same window described in rstudio/shiny#4400):

```r
library(shinytest2)

app_dir <- tempfile("announce-before-bind")
dir.create(app_dir)
writeLines(c(
  '# delay only the real bind (shiny probes for a free port with an empty app first)',
  'trace("startServer", where = asNamespace("shiny"), print = FALSE,',
  '      tracer = quote(if (length(app) > 0) Sys.sleep(5)))',
  'library(shiny)',
  'shinyApp(fluidPage("hello world"), function(input, output, session) {})'
), file.path(app_dir, "app.R"))

AppDriver$new(app_dir, load_timeout = 20000)
```

This aborts in ~6s (not at the 20s `load_timeout`) with `Shiny app did not become stable … Caused by error in app_wait_for_idle()`. Removing the `Sys.sleep()` removes only the determinism; the same failure then reproduces intermittently under load.

## Captured evidence (real CI failure)

CDP navigation/context lifecycle, times relative to the navigate:

```
   +56 ms   frameNavigated      -> chrome-error://chromewebdata/   (port not bound yet; error page)
   +88 ms   loadEventFired
 +2260 ms   executionContextsCleared
 +2263 ms   frameNavigated      -> http://127.0.0.1:5092/          (app now serving; error page recovers)
 +2280 ms   executionContextCreated
```

Two exceptions per attempt, both at `document.readyState === "loading"`, captured by tracing `chromote_eval()`:

```
init readiness check:  Error code: -32000   "Inspected target navigated or closed"   (page state: $/jQuery undefined — error page)
init idle check:       TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'log')  (page state: $/jQuery defined  — recovered app)
```

The change in page state between the two indicates the document was replaced between them.

## Why it surfaces as "did not become stable"

Once the navigation lands on the error page, three things line up:

1. The tracer (`shiny-tracer.js`) is [injected with a one-shot `chromote_eval()` right after `Page.navigate`](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3844574d93acfa6e3ae6fe25a41f5db5733ade2c/R/app-driver-initialize.R#L124-L135), so it lands on the error-page context. When the app binds and the browser recovers to the real document, that context is gone and the new document has no `window.shinytest2`.
2. The readiness wait's polling promise lives in the error-page context; the recovery navigation destroys it, and CDP rejects the evaluate with `-32000`. [`chromote_eval()` returns that under `results`](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3844574d93acfa6e3ae6fe25a41f5db5733ade2c/R/chromote-methods.R#L62-L71) (not `exceptionDetails`), while [`chromote_wait_for_condition()` only checks `exceptionDetails`](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3844574d93acfa6e3ae6fe25a41f5db5733ade2c/R/chromote-methods.R#L138-L140) — so the destroyed-context error is currently reported as a *successful* readiness. That false-success seems worth being aware of on its own, independent of the timing.
3. Initialization therefore proceeds to the idle check, whose [script opens with `window.shinytest2.log(...)`](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3844574d93acfa6e3ae6fe25a41f5db5733ade2c/R/app-driver-wait.R#L37). In the recovered context the tracer is absent, so it throws `reading 'log'`, which is surfaced and re-wrapped as "did not become stable".

## A possible fix

The most direct option found is to gate navigation on the port actually accepting a connection, rather than on the stderr line — e.g. poll `pingr::is_up(host, port)` (the reachability check [`app_httr2_get()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3844574d93acfa6e3ae6fe25a41f5db5733ade2c/R/httr2.R#L11) already uses) before navigating. I'm happy to supply a PR if this is a desirable direction to take.

title: `app$wait_for_value()` is broken using example app
description:
Running the example code from the package (below) currently results in a timeout. This seems to be a regression as it runs fine on v0.4.1.

`app$get_value(output = "total")` also fails with:

```
Error in `rlang::abort()`:
! `message` must be a character vector, not a <rlang_error> object.
```

Even though `app$get_values()` correctly contains:

```
$output$total
[1] "75"

```

```
library(shiny)
library(shinytest2)

shiny_app <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(
    h1("Dynamic output"),
    actionButton("display", "Display UI"),
    uiOutput("dym1"),
  ),
  function(input, output) {
    output$dym1 <- renderUI({
      req(input$display)
      Sys.sleep(runif(1, max = 2)) # Artificial calculations
      tagList(
        sliderInput("slider1", "Slider #1", 0, 100, 25),
        uiOutput("dym2")
      )
    })
    output$dym2 <- renderUI({
      Sys.sleep(runif(1, max = 2)) # Artificial calculations
      tagList(
        sliderInput("slider2", "Slider #2", 0, 100, 50),
        "Total:", verbatimTextOutput("total")
      )
    })
    output$total <- renderText({
      req(input$slider1, input$slider2)
      input$slider1 + input$slider2
    })
  }
)

app <- AppDriver$new(shiny_app)

# Create UI / output values
app$click("display")
# Wait for total to be calculated (or have a non-NULL value)
new_total_value <- app$wait_for_value(output = "total")
app$get_value(output = "total")
```

title: How to use local_app_support() with AppDriver
description:
Hello,

I have a shiny app that I want to test as part of a package. The app uses package functions, but currently I"m getting an error that the package is not found during test because it's not installed but loaded with devtools.

I read that the new `local_app_support()` function is designed to help here, but I don't know how to use it with a test app and the app driver. For example

```r
# App with modules
testApp <- shinyApp(
    ui <- fluidPage(
      mod_test_ui("test")
    ),
    server <- function(input, output, session) {
      mod_test_server(id = "test")
    }
  )

# Start app and click option 4
app <- AppDriver$new(app = testApp)
app$set_inputs("test-option" = "4")
```
This is not a fully reproducible example because you'd need the whole package, but where in this code do I add `local_app_support() ` such that I don't get the error: "packagename" not found, during testing. `local_app_support` requires an app_dir argument, but I don't have that given my app is passed as a variable to the AppDriver.

I hope I made the issue clear, but feel free to ask for more details!

Thanks

title: Rhandsontable dropdown functionality breaks in Shinytest2 browser (JS permissions policy violation)
description:
Hi, thanks as ever for the great package. I don't know how I managed without it.

I'm now trying to use Rhandsontable with dropdown options in a Shiny app (R 4.5.1, Shiny 1.11.0, Rhandsontable 0.3.8, Shinytest2 0.4.1). The table works fine in Chrome and Firefox, but when I try to record a test in the Shinytest2 browser session the dropdown cell fills stop working: specifically, I can open them, but not select an option or close them. I see there have been issues in Shinytest (not 2) about Rhandsontable cell validation failing, but nothing about dropdowns (though perhaps it's the same issue at root)?

I put together a minimal reprex:
```R app.r
library(shiny)
library(rhandsontable)

ui <- fluidPage(rHandsontableOutput("hot_table"))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$hot_table <- renderRHandsontable({
    df <- data.frame(Status = "Active")
    rhandsontable(df, height = 300) %>%
      hot_col("Status", type = "dropdown", source = c("Active", "Inactive"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

When I run `use_shinytest2(); record_test()` and then check the console in the Shinytest2 browser, I get the following error messages:
```JS

title: add helper to skip tests when some pkg is `pkgload::load_all()`d
description:
TL,DR: I have a `skip_if_installed_but_not_via_loadall(x = "my-in-dev-package")` helper, which helps me reduce the `load_all()`/installed package confusion: https://github.com/dataheld/elf/blob/main/R/installed.R

I'd be happy to contribute it, if you find it useful as a stop-gap until https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/issues/310 etc.

---

as I imagine some people who develop shiny apps as functions inside R packages, I kept shooting myself in the foot with [this](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/articles/use-package.html#other-setup-steps):

> [shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/) requires that your package to be installed when testing. [testthat::test_local()](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_package.html) (and related wrappers) eventually call [pkgload::load_all()](https://pkgload.r-lib.org/reference/load_all.html) to temporarily source the local R package. You can use [test_local()](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_package.html) to test non-[shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/) tests, but you will need to install your R package to safely execute your [shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/) tests. If not installed, it will create a confusing situation where your [shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/) tests are running on a different version of your R package (whichever was last installed), than the rest of your tests (the current source).

(as in, I confuse myself by running tests on the wrong version).

**As a stop-gap**, I've built myself a set of helpers to automatically skip (shinytest2) tests, whenever the package in question is currently (ie. when running the test) available via `pkgload::load_all()`.
This forces me to install the current version and then run `testthat::test_package(package = "mypkg", load_package = 'installed')`.
Even if I forget to install, `test_package()` I at least get the tests at the same version as the actual shiny app running.

The helpers to detect whether some package is currently `load_all()`d live [here](https://elf.maxheld.de/reference/pkg_installed_but_not_via_loadall):
They're just wrappers around `pkgload::is_dev_package()`.

The downside is that I have to provide a version of this for *every* package I built, since I couldn't figure out a way to find that name automatically.

(I also [tried](https://github.com/dataheld/niffler/pull/21) automatically figuring out all the used packages in an expression, and then looping over those to skip if *any* of them where `load_all()`d, but I couldn't make that work).

title: Remove internet dependencies.
description: When using wait_for_value() the function ends up calling app_httr_get() with in this function it calls pngr::is_up(). In the pngr documentation it states the check_online paramter for is_up() is defaulted to TRUE. This causes the user interface tests with wait_for_value() to fail with no internet connection and causes inconsistencies when running the tests due to internet speeds. Setting check_online = FALSE in this function would reduce false positives in the testing and also reduce the runtime of the testing suite.

title: `wait_for_value()`'s `ignore` logic uses overly strict `identical()` for comparison
description:
In this line, `wait_for_value()` is using `identical()` to compare the `ignore` parameter with the result of `$get_value()`

https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/799b11c2a86ef47cbaa0247ea9ce23f220e7c735/R/app-driver-wait.R#L133

This can lead to a situation where `wait_for_value()` doesn't actually wait if `ignore = 1` and `value = 1L` (i.e., `value` is an integer but `ignore` isn't). 

It seems better if the comparison was less strict, perhaps using `all.equal()` (similar to the difference between `expect_identical()` and `expect_equal()`)

Following up on rstudio/chromote#129, there are two things that shinytest2 can do:

1. When `selector = "viewport"`, shinytest2 can set `captureBeyondViewport = FALSE` for chromote's screenshot method.
2. When `selector = "scrollable_area"`, shinytest2 could query Chrome to determine how big the scrollable area is, then resize the viewport to match that size before screenshotting with `captureBeyondViewport = FALSE`, followed by restoring the viewport size.

   This option is more or less the pattern used by puppeteer, mentioned in https://github.com/rstudio/chromote/issues/96#issuecomment-1424642373.

title: GitHub Action: Load parent renv project when testing multiple apps via `app-dir` input
description:
I followed the example at [Using shinytest2 with continuous integration](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/articles/use-ci.html), with slight modifications:

```
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

name: Test app with renv

jobs:
  test-app:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}

    name: ${{ matrix.config.os }} (${{ matrix.config.r }})

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: ubuntu-latest, r: "4.3.1"}

    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: ${{ matrix.config.r }}
          use-public-rspm: true
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
      - uses: rstudio/shinytest2/actions/test-app@v1
        with:
          app-dir: |
            app
          upload-snapshots: true     
```

title: `get_download` fails with custom url
description:
I have a app that can take query parameters to set up some inputs. I am using the approach highlighted in https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/issues/219#issuecomment-1247161081 to test the app with the custom url. However, the `get_download` function fails and instead of downloading the correct file, downloads an html file. 

Here's a small reprex:

``` r
library(shiny)
library(shinytest2)

# sample test app
ui <- fluidPage(
    downloadButton("downloadData", "Download")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    # Our dataset
    data <- mtcars
    
    output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
        filename = function() {
            paste("data-", Sys.Date(), ".csv", sep="")
        },
        content = function(file) {
            write.csv(data, file)
        }
    )
}

my_app <- shinyApp(ui, server)

# Test with base URL
test_app1 <- AppDriver$new(my_app)
test_app1$get_download('downloadData', 'temp_file.csv')
#> ./temp_file.csv

# reads correctly
head(read.csv("temp_file.csv"))
#>                   X  mpg cyl disp  hp drat    wt  qsec vs am gear carb
#> 1         Mazda RX4 21.0   6  160 110 3.90 2.620 16.46  0  1    4    4
#> 2     Mazda RX4 Wag 21.0   6  160 110 3.90 2.875 17.02  0  1    4    4
#> 3        Datsun 710 22.8   4  108  93 3.85 2.320 18.61  1  1    4    1
#> 4    Hornet 4 Drive 21.4   6  258 110 3.08 3.215 19.44  1  0    3    1
#> 5 Hornet Sportabout 18.7   8  360 175 3.15 3.440 17.02  0  0    3    2
#> 6           Valiant 18.1   6  225 105 2.76 3.460 20.22  1  0    3    1

# Test with custom URL
current_url <- test_app1$get_url()
test_app2 <- AppDriver$new(paste0(current_url, "?foo=bar"))
test_app2$get_download("downloadData", "temp_file.csv")
#> ./temp_file.csv

# HTML file gets downloaded
readLines("temp_file.csv", 5) 
#> [1] "<!DOCTYPE html>"                                                           
#> [2] "<html>"                                                                    
#> [3] "<head>"                                                                    
#> [4] "  <meta http-equiv=\"Content-Type\" content=\"text/html; charset=utf-8\"/>"
#> [5] "  <script type=\"application/shiny-singletons\"></script>"
```

<sup>Created on 2023-09-29 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I believe the issue seems to be within `app_download` function when it generates the `full_url`
https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/176131dc1bb1bd2510100484131bb2f130dd7d99/R/app-driver-expect-download.R#L22

In my case this becomes `http://127.0.0.1:4895/?foo=barsession/d7b1669e84114236fc18752d3fd5c547/download/downloadData?w=` . If I modify this to remove the query part `http://127.0.0.1:4895/session/d7b1669e84114236fc18752d3fd5c547/download/downloadData?w=`, then the download works as expected. 

As a temporary fix, I am opening the app with the custom URL so that the app can use the query parameters while loading and before downloading, set the url manually to remove the query part. 

``` r

But this is not desirable. Is there a better way until there's a fix?

title: Cannot run tests unless connected to internet
description:
When not connected to internet (or when behind a proxy) tests cannot run because `app$expect_values()` returns an error. The error comes from `app_httr_get`:
```r
library(shiny)
library(shinytest2)
#> Loading required package: testthat

ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput("name", "What is your name?"),
  actionButton("greet", "Greet"),
  textOutput("greeting")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$greeting <- renderText({
    req(input$greet)
    paste0("Hello ", isolate(input$name), "!")
  })
}
shiny_app <- shinyApp(ui, server)

app <- AppDriver$new(shiny_app)
app$set_inputs(name = "Hugo")
app$click("greet")
app$expect_values()
#> Error in `app_httr_get()`:
#> ! Could not find Shiny server. Shiny app is no longer running
#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. └─app$expect_values()
#>  2.   └─shinytest2:::app_expect_values(...)
#>  3.     └─shinytest2:::app_httr_get(...)
#>  4.       └─shinytest2:::app_abort(self, private, "Could not find Shiny server. Shiny app is no longer running")
#>  5.         └─rlang::abort(..., app = self, call = call)
``` 
Created on 2023-07-11 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/)

And this is actually due to [the call](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/6850de4a421fd592873e638d6deda8a4fd176660/R/httr.R#L11C15-L11C21) to `pingr::is_up` to check if the server is running. By the default, `pingr::is_up` checks first if the computer is online (`check_online = TRUE`).

In my case, since I work behind a proxy, this means I cannot use shinytest2 at all. So shouldn't be `pingr::is_up` called with `check_online = FALSE` to prevent this situation?

I can create a pull request if needed.

Thanks for the great package!

title: Capture reactives from a Shiny app in a general way
description:
Love the package. Currently inputs and outputs can be automatically exported. Creating issue to see if there is a way to generally export all reactives without explicitly declaring them in `shiny::exportTestValues()`. This could be a future feature. Here is a reproducible example in this direction:
``` r
library(shiny)
library(shinytest2)
shiny_app <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(
    h1("Pythagorean theorem"),
    numericInput("A", "A", 3),
    numericInput("B", "B", 4),
    verbatimTextOutput("C"),
  ),
  function(input, output) {
    a_squared <- reactive({ req(input$A); input$A * input$A })
    b_squared <- reactive({ req(input$B); input$B * input$B })
    c_squared <- reactive({ a_squared() + b_squared() })
    c_value <- reactive({ sqrt(c_squared()) })
    
    output$C <- renderText({ c_value() })
    

    observe({
      # alternatively, automatically generate list of reactives for export
      # use function to auto gen reactive list
      getReactives4Export <- function(n = 3) {
        # note that function is expected to run within a reactive context
        # get parent environment
        curr_env <- rlang::env_parent(n = n)
        reactive_objs <-
          unlist(lapply(curr_env, shiny::is.reactive))
        export <- names(reactive_objs[reactive_objs == T])

        # omit the get_inputs reactive which is used for loading purposes
        # can also omit other reactives as needed here
        export <- export[export != "get_inputs"]
        # wrangle export vector into list with reactive formatting
        export_names <- export
        export <- as.list(export)
        # print TRUE or FALSE to the developers console depending on if
        # reactives were captured
        if (length(export) > 0) {
          print("export success")
          export <- paste0(export, "()")
        } else{
          print("export fail")
          export
        }
        names(export) <- export_names
        # parse list reactives to get objects
        eval_parse_reactive <-
          function(reactive_str) {
            eval(parse(text = reactive_str))
          }
        export_vals <- lapply(export, eval_parse_reactive)
        # another idea would be also saving reactive expressions
        ## interesting idea I first saw in shinyobjects (https://rjake.github.io/shinyobjects/)
        ## this export_expr line of code gets those expressions into a list
        export_expr <- lapply(names(export), eval_parse_reactive)
        return(export_vals)
      }
      all_reactives <- getReactives4Export()
      exportTestValues(
        all_reactives = all_reactives
      )
    })
    
})

app <- AppDriver$new(shiny_app)

init_vals <- app$get_values()
str(init_vals)
#> List of 3
#>  $ input :List of 2
#>   ..$ A: int 3
#>   ..$ B: int 4
#>  $ output:List of 1
#>   ..$ C: chr "5"
#>  $ export:List of 1
#>   ..$ all_reactives:List of 4
#>   .. ..$ c_value  : num 5
#>   .. ..$ c_squared: int 25
#>   .. ..$ b_squared: int 16
#>   .. ..$ a_squared: int 9
```

description:
### Summary 
It seems that in the current version of `set_inputs` one has to hard-code the input components. 

### App and evaluation
Please find a simple app with example uses of `set_input` below:
```r
library(shinytest2) 

two_radio_buttons_app <- shinyApp(ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("rd1", "rd1", letters[1:5]),
  radioButtons("rd2", "rd2", LETTERS[1:5]),
  textOutput("rd_out")
  
),
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$rd_out <-
    renderText(sprintf("info: rd1:%s rd2:%s", input$rd1, input$rd2))
  
})

app <- shinytest2::AppDriver$new(two_radio_buttons_app, name = "two_radio_buttons_app")
on.exit({
  print(app$get_logs())
  app$stop()
  rm(app)
})

test_that("evaluate `set_input`", {
  print("### providing input component as hard-coded data")
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
  app$set_inputs(rd1 = "b")
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
  app$set_inputs(rd1 = "e")
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
  
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd2"))
  app$set_inputs(rd2 = "C")
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd2"))
  app$set_inputs(rd2 = "D")
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd2"))
  
  print("### providing input component as variables")
  rd1_v1 <- "b"
  rd1_id <- "rd1"
  rd1_v2 <- "c"
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
  
  # value can be provided as variable
  app$set_inputs("rd1" = rd1_v1)
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
  
  # input component can be provided as variable (solution #1)
  app$set_inputs(`as.name(rd1_id)` = rd1_v2)
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
  
  # input component can be provided as variable (solution #2)
  rv <- structure(rd1_v2, names = rd1_id)
  app$set_inputs(rv)
  print(app$get_value(input = "rd1"))
})

title: record_test() does not work with Shiny.setInputValue() when given a dictionary of values
description:
When custom javascript creates an input using `Shiny.setInputValue(key, value)`, it works fine if the value is a single value. But when provided with a dictionary, it does not record the keys and only records the values.

Example:

```
library(shiny)

app <- shinyApp(
   fluidPage(
     div(
       "click me",
       onclick = "Shiny.setInputValue('test', { 'key1' : 'val1', 'key2' : 'val2' }, {priority: 'event'})"
     ),
     verbatimTextOutput("test")
   ),
   
   function(input, output, session) {
     output$test <- renderPrint({
       str(input$test)
     }) 
   }
)

driver <- shinytest2::AppDriver$new(app)

shinytest2::record_test(driver)
```

Press on the div that says "click me", which triggers a javascript input being set. When the modal asking if to record or ignore comes up, click "Record".  The result is:

```r
app$set_inputs(test = c("val1", "val2"), allow_no_input_binding_ = TRUE, priority_ = "event")
```

Which is incorrect. It should be 

```r
app$set_inputs(test = c("jey1" = "val1", "key2" = "val2"), allow_no_input_binding_ = TRUE, priority_ = "event")
```

title: `{testthat}` file loading
description:
Making an issue to consolidate conversation.

## Bug
* Dev code is not loaded in background Shiny R session
* Unwanted as it requires package authors to install before testing

## Approaches
* Use `{future}`
	* `{future}` does not capture logging very well. Requires the Shiny app to shut down to get the output logs
		* This is a deal breaker
	* `{future}` does do a good job of capturing the dev R code
* Use testthat code loading
	* Need to inspect `testthat::test_local(load_package=)`
		* Maybe a flag could be passed through to tell the Shiny R session to load code this way
		* When `load_package="source"`, it eventually calls `testthat:::test_files_setup_env()` which calls a ramped up version of `pkgload::load_all()`

## Resolution
Ideally, all labels with `theme: testthat file loading` could be resolved

description:
[The documentation](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/articles/use-package.html#other-setup-steps) for using shinytest2 with a packaged shiny app states that "[shinytest2](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest2/) requires that your package to be installed when testing".
Could you confirm whether or not this is still the case, please. 

If I set up a leprechaun app
```
usethis::create_package("tempGreeter")
leprechaun::scaffold()
devtools::document()
```

with UI/server:
```r
ui = function(req) {
  fluidPage(
    textOutput("greeting")
  )
}

server = function(input, output, session) {
  output$greeting <- renderText({
    paste0("Hello, World!")
  })
}
```

Then add shinytest2 infrastructure
```
shinytest2::use_shinytest2()
```

Then add a simple test:
```
# ./tests/testthat/test-e2e-greeting.R
test_that("it displays 'Hello World!'", {
  shiny_app = tempGreeter::run()
  app = shinytest2::AppDriver$new(shiny_app, name = "greeter")

  app$expect_values(screenshot_args = FALSE)
})
```

A) Without installing the package, the test runs and passes using either `devtools::test()` at the console or in the RStudio Build window
B) On installing the package (`devtools::install()`), the test runs and passes as well (either using the R console or the RStudio build window)
C) On changing the package so that output$greeting renders "Hello, Earth!", but without installing the new version of the package, the test fails because of a mismatch between the "Hello Earth!" in the uninstalled package's source code, and the expected "Hello World!" stored in the snapshots.

Is there a subtlety that I've missed? There didn't seem to be a setting where the installed version of the package was used preferentially over the working version when running tests.

  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

        r: [4.2.1]
    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes
    steps:
      - name: Install linux system dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash

In line with that, `shiny`s changelog says
> When taking a test snapshot, the sort order of the json keys of the input, output, and export fields is currently sorted using the locale of the machine. This can lead to inconsistent test snapshot results. To opt-in to a consistent ordering of snapshot fields with {shinytest}, please set the global option options(shiny.snapshotsortc = TRUE). **{shinytest2} users do not need to set this value.** (#3515)

This is somewhat of a breaking change for `shinytest2` users. Is there an easy way of reverting this, or is this hard-coded? I tried setting `options(shiny.snapshotsortc = TRUE)`, but without effect - it may be that `shinytest2` is overriding it in line 279:

https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/08c4060609d5ee9b52278521a08cbf4e0593ffb4/R/app-driver-expect-values.R#L273-L281

title: Use desktop mode by using a user agent
description:

> Yep, I had a very similar issue. The first thing you need to do is manually identify your user agent, check out [this site](https://www.whatismybrowser.com/detect/what-is-my-user-agent). For example, your user agent could be a long string describing a Safari browser running on macOS that renders web pages using the WebKit engine.
> 
> Now go ahead and add in an option to manually set your user agent
> 
> ```
> options.add_argument("user-agent=User-Agent: your user agent string here")
> ```
> 
> An example might look like this:

title: Incorect code coverage using `covr` on `shinytest2` + `testthat` tests
description:
I've encountered a problem during calculation of code coverage using `covr`. Even though the tests scripts were executing lines, they were not appearing in the results of `covr::package_coverage()`.

Issue was reported [there](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/438), and it seems like, as the answer [here](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/438#issuecomment-1230350786) points out, the `app_stop()` is executing SIGKILL too soon for `covr` to trace the lines.

Using [this answer](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/277#issuecomment-555502769) as a guidelines, I was able to countermeasure this problem using a simple function that is executed before calling `app$stop()`:

```r
app_wait <- function(app,
                     time = 1000) {
  
  app$.__enclos_env__$private$shiny_process$interrupt()
  app$.__enclos_env__$private$shiny_process$wait(timeout = time)
}
```

I suggest either upping the time before the `SIGKILL` execution or providing the user an option to overwrite this time.

title: `AppDriver$wait_for_js()` does not quote script input
description:
The `eval()` call in the `chromote_wait_for_condition ` function is essentially a NOP instruction as the `condition_js ` script is not quoted: https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/61d51d9e96640bfae3eeefa12c4b685099b584c8/R/chromote-methods.R#L105
This leads to e.g. the input script `'test'==='test';` throwing a Javascript error:  `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ';'. Expected ')' to end an argument list.` as the code to be executed looks like this: `eval('test'==='test';)` which is obviously invalid syntax.
To fix this, the `condition_js` needs to be quoted properly.

title: Url R6Class set method builds and sets an incorrect URL when query parameters with no value are passed
description:
### Code to reproduce:
```
url <- shinytest2::Url$new()
url$set("http://127.0.0.1:1234/?_inputs_&n=10")
url$get()
# Returned value: [1] "http://127.0.0.1:1234/?_inputs_=&n=10"
# Expected value: [1] "http://127.0.0.1:1234/?_inputs_&n=10"
# Notice the '=' after '_inputs_' in the returned value
```

### Origin:
The origin of the bug can be pinpointed to:
https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/29c7a6b2cfc83de720acc5ca86cdab73dca7ad0e/R/R6-helper.R#L60

This function receives the following value in `res`:
```
$scheme
[1] "http"

$hostname
[1] "127.0.0.1"

$port
[1] "1234"

$path
[1] ""

$query
$query$`_inputs_`
[1] ""

$query$n
[1] "10"


$params
NULL

$fragment
NULL

$username
NULL

$password
NULL

attr(,"class")
[1] "url"
```
It treats `_inputs_` as a query parameter (in fact it is one but it has a special meaning in shiny) and tries to reconstructs it as such.

### Possible approaches for solutions

I am unsure if the behavior of `httr::build_url` is the expected one as it does not return `_inputs_=""`, but only `_inputs_=`. There are no particular specifications for this case in the reference doc in https://httr.r-lib.org/reference/parse_url.html

Fixing it locally would imply treating `_inputs_` query parameter as a special case. Unsure of the best approach as introducing `_inputs_` may not be trivial as it may not may be in some cases placed immediately after '/?'. And grepping and replacing can be dangerous as it could match things like `http::127.0.0.1:1234/?_inputs_&conflicting_input='_inputs_='`.

### Relevance
This will very likely have a direct impact in the enhancement proposed in #219

title: Rounded corners are not consistent
description:
Related rstudio/shinytest2#136
Related rstudio/shinytest2#4 
Related rstudio/chromote#96

Rounded corners are not being produced consistently on the same platforms. Shadows and borders are particularly difficult as they are being calculated with a bit of randomness. I believe this is due to inconsistent sub pixel rounding and/or snapping.

Related chromium issues: 
* Issue 937273: Different rounding for subpixel border vs outline - https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=937273&q=subpixel%20snapping&can=2
* Issue 1313330: Color picker's border displays incorrectly in high contrast mode - https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1313330
* Issue 1267773: One-off pixel error on layer  - https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1267773#c9

This was originally addressed in rstudio/shinytest2#136 by not adjusting the screen size within `{chromote}`. While the output cards were addressed, the change in `{chromote}` did not fix _all_ rounded corner issues.

Example: 

See red corners of both the modal and focused text in the image below. Red color means that a difference was found using the command `gm compare old.png new.png -highlight-style assign -file diff.png`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93231/171919539-4b7d4905-e221-4918-b3a4-bb01de20a108.png)

-----------------------------------------------------

Proposal: 

Add a `compare` function to `AppDriver$expect_sreenshot(compare=)`. Add a new comparison method that computes a "difference" metric and compare it against a set threshold.

The current compare function is set to `testthat::compare_file_binary(old, new)`. 

Proposed `shinytest2::image_threshold(threshold = 0, size = 100)` algorithm:
* Compare images using `testthat::compare_file_binary()`
	* If successful, return success
* Read in red, green, blue changes of each file
* Find abs differences in each channel for each file
* If threshold  == 0 || size <= 1
	* Return `sum(abs_diffs) == 0`
* Run convolution over diff matrix using a kernal w/ width and height set to `size`
* `total = sum(convo_vals)`
* Return `total < threshold`


-----------------------

Implementation would be done using `{cpp11}`.

title: Add an `$expect()` method to keep the method chain alive
description:
Method chaining expectactions, especially for complicated app interactions, can be really helpful. Also with judicious use of `$wait_for_js()`, you can make sure your tests don't get ahead of your app.

(Note this is mostly just me thinking out loud.)

## Motivation

Imagine you're testing an app that includes a modal. You want to test that:

1. Clicking a button in the standard UI opens the modal
2. The modal opens
3. It has a particular class
4. It has a "save" button that is disabled
5. Changing an input value in the modal dialogue enables the save button
6. Clicking the save button closes the modal
7. The original button has a check mark icon to indicate the change

What's important is that each step only makes sense if the previous steps were completed successfully. We also want to occasionally wait to give the app time to think or animate a state change.

## Psuedo-code

In pseudo-code (mostly hiding the JavaScript code), with an `$expect()` method that invisibly yields the `app` object, one could write code like this.

```r
app <- AppDriver$new("app.R")

app$
  click(selector = "#open-modal")$
  wait_for_js(modal_state_is("open"))$
  expect("succeed", "modal was opened")$
  expect("true", get_js(selector_has_class("#modal", "primary"))$
  expect("true", get_js(selector_exists("#modal .btn-save"))$
  expect(
    "equal",
    get_js(selector_classlist("#modal .btn-save")),
    list("btn", "btn-save", "disabled")
  )$
  expect(
    "equal",
    get_text(selector = "#modal .btn-save"),
    "Save Changes (Disabled)"
  )$
  set_inputs(enable_save = TRUE)$
  expect("equal", get_js(selector_classlist("#modal .btn-save")), list("btn", "btn-save"))$
  expect("equal", get_text(selector = "#modal .btn-save"), "Save Changes")$
  click(selector = "#modal .btn-save")$
  wait_for_js(modal_state_is("closed"))$
  expect("succeed", "modal was closed")$
  expect("match", get_html(selector = "#open-modal"), '<i class="fa fas-check">')
```

## Sketch

Here's a sketch of an `$expect()` method

```r
shinytest2::AppDriver$set("public", "expect", function(name, object, expected, ...) {
  stopifnot(length(name) == 1)
  name <- tolower(name)
  if (identical(name, "succeed")) {
    testthat::succeed(...)
    return(invisible(self))
  }
  
  allowed_expectactions <- c(
    "null", "true", "false", "equal", "length", "match", "no_match", "setequal"
  )
  
  if (!name %in% allowed_expectactions) {
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "'%s' is not one of the supported expectations: %s",
      name,
      paste(allowed_expectactions, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
  
  dots <- list(...)
  self_mask <- rlang::new_data_mask(self)

  if (!missing(object)) {
    object <- rlang::enquo(object)
    dots$object <- rlang::eval_tidy(object, self_mask)
  }
  if (!missing(expected)) {
    expected <- rlang::enquo(expected)
    dots$expected <- rlang::eval_tidy(expected, self_mask)
  }

  call <- rlang::call2(.fn = paste0("expect_", name), !!!dots, .ns = "testthat")
  rlang::eval_bare(call)

  invisible(self)
})
```

title: Package option for `wait_for_*()` timeouts
description:
If you're using a lot of `$wait_for_js()` calls, 30 seconds is a massively long timeout, and it'd be nice to be able to set a global option for the default timeout, e.g.

```r
options(shinytest2.wait_for_js.timeout = 5 * 1000)
```

instead of having to include `timeout = 5 * 1000` in all of my calls to `$wait_for_js()`. I would imagine heavy users of other `wait_for_*()` functions would benefit from similar options.

An alternative would be to lower the timeout for all of the wait functions to something reasonably small, e.g. 5 or 10 seconds, and then users who know they need to wait longer can opt into a longer wait time. (And I guess you'd also use longer timeouts for app startup.)

```
library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)
library(shinytest2)

app <- shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),
    actionButton("reset", "reset"),
    textInput("text", "text", "text")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    observeEvent(input$reset, reset("text"))
  }
)

driver <- AppDriver$new(app)
driver$set_inputs(text = "text2")
driver$click("reset")
str(driver$get_values())
```

The result is this:

```
List of 3
 $ input :List of 3
  ..$ reset                  : int 1
  ..$ shinyjs-resettable-text:List of 1
  .. ..$ text:List of 2
  .. .. ..$ type : chr "Text"
  .. .. ..$ value: chr "text"
  ..$ text                   : chr "text"
 $ output: Named list()
 $ export: Named list()
```

You can see the `shinyjs-resettable-text` input. In this case it's small, but it'll have a value for each input in the app that was ever reset. When doing snapshots and trying to compare/verify, it can get very noisy to have these sort of inputs in there, where in practice they are useless. Would be great if there was a way to ignore these.

title: Idea: `AppDriver$new(combine_set_inputs=TRUE)` to combine consecutive lines of `set_inputs()` into one
description:
To achieve smaller/arguably more readable and clear test scripts.

I just created a small app with a bunch of inputs and wanted to change all of them, and then click a button. This is the result:

```
  app <- AppDriver$new()
  app$set_inputs(slider = 5)
  app$set_inputs(radio = "d")
  app$set_inputs(radio2 = "c")
  app$set_inputs(date2 = c("2010-02-21", "2010-05-23"))
  app$set_inputs(datetime2 = c(1271664000, 1279317600))
  app$set_inputs(datetime2 = c(1275069600, 1282723200))
  app$set_inputs(datetime = 1276855200)
  app$set_inputs(date = "2010-06-23")
  app$set_inputs(text = "text2")
  app$set_inputs(num = 1)
  app$set_inputs(num = 10)
  app$click("reset")
```

There certainly are cases where it might be important to set inputs separately, for example if there's a `reactiveVal()` that depends on each input change. But there are also many instances where I would argue it's nicer for the developer to get one command to look at instead of all that.  It makes it a little easier to manually add/remove/modify setting inputs as well.

```
  app <- AppDriver$new()
  app$set_inputs(
    slider = 5,
    radio = "d",
    radio2 = "c",
    date2 = c("2010-02-21", "2010-05-23"),
    datetime2 = c(1271664000, 1279317600),
    datetime2 = c(1275069600, 1282723200),
    datetime = 1276855200,
    date = "2010-06-23",
    text = "text2",
    num = 1,
    num = 10

```

title: Testing in the IDE ; Using `./tests/testthat/setup.R`
description:
Currently, clicking "Run tests" in the corner will not call `shinytest2::test_app()` in `./tests/testthat.R`.

TIL about `tests/testthat/setup.R` which is run before any test file is run, similar to a helper file. 

I am wondering if:

* `test_app()` should NOT be the boiler plate code for `./tests/testthat.R` and instead it should be similar to `testthat::test_dir("testthat")`
* `./tests/testthat/setup.R` should always exist and should be filled some form of: `shiny::loadSupport("../../", renv = rlang::current_env(), globalenv = rlang::current_env())`
* Each time a snapshot function is run, that function does a local call to set `{testthat}` edition 3. There is no need to force users to use `{testthat}` edition 3 as long as the snapshot can be taken.  ("What if there is a snapshot edition 4?!?". Locally setting the edition would resolve this issue.)

* `test_app(app_dir=)` could be removed in favor of `shiny::runTests(app_dir)` or `testthat::test_dir(file.path(app_dir, "tests", "testthat"))`

---------------

Pros:
* Fixes "Run tests" button
* Fits into the assumption that `./tests/testthat.R` is only `testthat::test_dir("testthat")`

Cons:
* Adds an additional file `setup.R` for every app being tracked. This seems verbose / unnecessary when it could be handled by `shinytest::test_app()` in `./tests/testthat.R`
* I find `shiny::runTests()` to be clunky over `testthat::test_dir()`

------------------

Please chime in with thoughts!

title: Should `$get_value()` be implemented using `$get_all_values()`?
description:
`$get_value()` executes javascript to ask the browser and reach into the implementation details information about the object.  To use this method, the widget type must be **white listed** to particular inputs/outputs.

`$get_all_values()` asks the shiny server for a JSON representation of all input/output/export types.  This works for **all widgets** that shiny can display.

------------------------------

`$get_value()` is rigid and does not allow for shiny to update its implementation details. 

Questions
* Should `$get_value(name, "input")` actually call `$get_all_values(input = name, output = FALSE, export = FALSE)`?
* Should `{shiny}` add `set_input_value(name, value)` (or a url endpoint) when in testing mode? I believe this is related to https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/issues/28

title: `shinytest2` approach to saving/comparing images
description:
This issue is to propose a new approach to how images are store/compared in an attempt to dramatically reduce the number of snapshot file, reducing overall confusion.

----------------------------------

*  Current approach: 
    * Store all snaps in `_snaps/OS-RVersion/TEST/XYZ.{json,png}`
    * Checking:
        * Given an OS/RVersion, the json and images much match perfectly
    * Pros:
        * Get json/images for each and every OS/RVersion combo
        * Can have different, known output for different OS/RVersions
    * Cons:
        * More files to maintain. Becomes unwieldily very quickly with many tests
        * Hard to see differences between images within the same test

* New approach: 
    * Store all snaps in `_snaps/TEST/XYZ.{json,png}` (No _variant_)
    * Store the _master_ version meta information in `_shinytest2.json`. Info such as `OS` and `RVersion`.
    * Checking:
        * If the OS/RVersion match exactly, then all images / json should **match perfectly**
        * Else, all images/json should be able to **fuzzy match**
            * Image fuzzy matching should be similar to https://github.com/MangoTheCat/visualTest . Inspiration: https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest/issues/412
            * JSON:
                * Maybe the HTML SHA should never be compared?
                * Maybe the image SHA should never be compared?
                * Maybe we fuzzy match the information?
    * Pros:
        * Minimal number of files to maintain; 1:1 ratio of json/images to expected snapshots
        * Do not let snapshots from other platforms slip through the cracks as long as the master version exists.
          Example using the "current approach" above: Init on mac and then test on linux. This situation will never throw on differences
          However, using fuzzy matching, you can init on mac and then immediately test on linux using fuzzy matching.
          Shinycoreci-apps ran into this due to maintenance fatigue and accepting images right away. Then not being able to compare json/images between OS/RVersions allowed the image to survive longer than it should have.
    * Cons:
        * Exact images for all flavors are not known. Only the _master_ version
        * Small display issues in other OS/RVersions will not be caught. Ex: Let's say linux displays sliders using dark grey, while the master version displays them with light grey. The fuzzy match will say that it is tolerable, while it might actually be an issue.
          If this is the case, the tolerance could be set to `0`, but would have be manually done.

* `st2_expect_html()`:
    * Testing functions like `st2_expect_html()` would also be bundled into this situation. 
    * I would argue that `st2_expect_html()` should not have fuzzy matching by default. Maybe it should be run through `tagQuery()` (or something similar) to produce consistent output. Ex: `attribs$class` names and `attribs` keys are in a consistent order.

---------------

@wch What are your thoughts? 

I believe this is a win/win in that we get less images to maintain and we also get to fuzzy match when testing on differing OS/RVersions. (Exact matching on the _master_ OS/RVersion; Fuzzy matching on all other OS/RVersions.) This would also allow for Linux machines to be _bold_ and _not bold_ and not provide false-positive results in shinycoreci-apps.
